title: Step 1. The simple model: identical agents, α and β set
html:
Step 1. The simple model: identical agents, α and β set

Question: On a generated idea graph, at step 1 of the model, how far does a society get for the same money, by α and β?

Answer: Best overall: OSO (α = 0.8, β = 1). Against traditional, clearly better on hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level and waste. (8 measures; a clear difference is more than 2.7 standard errors.)

  • hardest level: 6.00 against traditional 0.36, clearly better.
  • targets solved: 2.00 against traditional 0.07, clearly better.
  • bounty value: 256 against traditional 8.96, clearly better.
  • ROI: 0.65 against traditional 0.01, clearly better.
  • knowledge found (bits): 101 against traditional 60, clearly better.
  • knowledge per unit of money: 0.25 against traditional 0.05, clearly better.
  • money to the main level: 283 against traditional 964, clearly better.
  • waste: 0.32 against traditional 0.72, clearly better.

Design (fixed before the run): compared α in {1, 0.8, 0.2} × β in {0, 1} · held the same: a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7), 12 identical agents, equal money each round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation (θ = 0), a budget of 1200 · measure: all of hardest level, targets solved, bounty value, ROI, knowledge found (bits), knowledge per unit of money, money to the main level, waste · 100 runs per row.

Caveats:

  • A simulation with guessed parameters: it shows how the rules play out, not that they work.
Details

Step 1 of the model step by step (the simple model) on a generated idea graph (6 levels × 8 ideas, 2 parents each, sequences of 3 bits growing by 2 per level, composition 0.7); each run draws its own graph. Only α and β vary. Held fixed: 12 identical agents, equal money each round (f = 0), no flat mint, a knowledge reward of 1 per new bit flowing back with α, no validation (θ = 0), a budget of 1200.

Values are mean ± standard deviation over runs.
